title: Enemy health-bar FSM diagram disagrees with EnemyHealthBarWidget.cpp, which has two freeze bugs
instrument: UE functional test: damage during FadingIn and death while Visible, assert render opacity reaches 1 / 0; plus an app test pinning TRANSITIONS to the chosen FSM
body:
## Summary
EnemyHealthBarFSM.tsx draws Visible->FadingIn on re-damage and three death shortcuts to Hidden; the UE widget does neither, and the widget itself freezes in two of those paths.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/EnemyHealthBarFSM.tsx:48 draws Visible->FadingIn (reset). EnemyHealthBarWidget.cpp OnHealthChanged (UE project Source/PoF/UI/EnemyHealthBarWidget.cpp:241-252) keeps Visible and only resets the timer; it also sends a FadingIn bar to Visible, which never calls SetRenderOpacity, so the bar freezes at a partial alpha. src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/EnemyHealthBarFSM.tsx:50-52 draw death as a jump to Hidden; HideForDeath (EnemyHealthBarWidget.cpp:215-226) sets FadingOut, but NativeTick returns early on bDead (EnemyHealthBarWidget.cpp:86), so the fade never runs and a dead enemy keeps its bar. Which runtime is right is an authority decision (cross-runtime-rules-conformance, divergence-log-not-silent-correction), and the UE fix lives in another repository.

## Flow
- Damage a visible enemy: diagram shows FadingIn; C++ stays Visible
- Damage an enemy mid fade-in: C++ jumps to Visible at alpha < 1 and stays translucent
- Kill an enemy whose bar is visible: C++ sets FadingOut, tick returns on bDead, bar never fades
- Fix: decide the intended FSM, fix the C++ (let FadingOut tick when bDead, keep FadingIn on re-damage), then redraw the diagram from it

## Expected impact
Designers read a diagram that matches the shipped widget, and dead enemies lose their bar. Could break UE functional tests that pin the current states.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - diagram and widget agree, and the widget has no frozen states
Before: 3 of 9 diagram transitions disagree with the C++ (Visible->FadingIn, FadingIn->Hidden, Visible->Hidden); 2 C++ paths freeze opacity
After: predicted 0 disagreements and 0 frozen paths once the intended FSM is chosen
Method: simulation - walked the C++ OnHealthChanged/HideForDeath/NativeTick by hand; no UE run in this round (operator-only act, other repository)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Damage-number sandbox lays mobs out on a fixed 520px while the canvas is 100% wide
instrument: renderHook + mocked ResizeObserver reporting 900px: assert mobMarkers[0].x === 450
body:
## Summary
useDamageNumberPhysicsSimulator hard-codes canvasW = 520 for mob spacing and spawn x, but SimulationCanvas renders width 100%, and canvasRef is never read.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/DamageNumberPhysicsSimulator/useDamageNumberPhysicsSimulator.ts:28 canvasW = 520 drives mobSpacing in simulation.ts spawnParticle and mobMarkers. src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/DamageNumberPhysicsSimulator/SimulationCanvas.tsx:62-66 sets width: 100%. canvasRef is attached (SimulationCanvas.tsx:61) but .current is read nowhere (grep: 0 reads). On a 900px column one mob sits at x=260 instead of 450, so the readability numbers are measured on a crowded left part of the canvas.

## Flow
- Open Damage Numbers on a wide window, 1 mob
- Mob marker and numbers sit left of centre
- Fix: ResizeObserver on canvasRef feeds canvasW state; spawn and markers read it

## Expected impact
Mobs centre at any width and clutter numbers reflect the real spread. Could shift preset clutter scores.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - mob layout matches the rendered canvas width
Before: mob 1 x = 260px regardless of canvas width (900px canvas: 190px off centre)
After: predicted x = width/2 at every width
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Readability metrics are mislabeled: "max" and "avg" are one-frame counts
instrument: pure test feeding computeReadability-style accumulator a 3-frame sequence and asserting peak/mean
body:
## Summary
computeReadability returns the current frame count as maxSimultaneous and a pair count as avgOverlaps, with a fixed 25px overlap test that ignores font size.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/DamageNumberPhysicsSimulator/simulation.ts:174 maxSimultaneous = visible.length (this frame only, not a max). The returned avgOverlaps is a raw pair count for one frame. simulation.ts:170 counts an overlap at dist < 25 for 18px and 26px text alike, so a crit-heavy preset under-counts real overlaps. The tiles (SimulationCanvas.tsx Overlaps / Simultaneous) flicker every frame instead of summarising a run.

## Flow
- Run AoE Stress Test preset
- Simultaneous tile flickers frame to frame; never shows the peak
- Fix: keep a running peak and a windowed mean in the hook; overlap test by text box (fontSize x scale)

## Expected impact
Designers read stable, honest numbers. Changes the clutterScore inputs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - metric names match what they compute
Before: maxSimultaneous equals the last frame count (walked: 3 frames 4,7,5 -> shows 5)
After: predicted peak 7, mean 5.3
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Tailwind arbitrary hex classes escape the no-hex ESLint rule
instrument: ESLint RuleTester case with className="bg-[#03030a]" expected to warn
evidence:
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/MenuFlowDiagram/index.tsx:52 bg-[#03030a]
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/MenuFlowDiagram/index.tsx:136 focus:ring-offset-[#03030a]
eslint: ScreenEditor.tsx:79, TransitionList.tsx:59 only
body:
## Summary
MenuFlowDiagram/index.tsx uses bg-[#03030a] and focus:ring-offset-[#03030a]; ESLint reports the two style-string hexes in this context but not these.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/MenuFlowDiagram/index.tsx:52 and :136 carry #03030a inside className. npx eslint over the context reports hex warnings only at ScreenEditor.tsx:79 and TransitionList.tsx:59 (string literals in style), so the rule misses hex inside arbitrary-value classes. The fix is in the ESLint rule (outside this context), then the two sites move to a token.

## Flow
- npx eslint src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/MenuFlowDiagram -> 2 hex warnings, none on index.tsx
- Extend the no-restricted-syntax hex selector to match /\[#[0-9a-f]{3,8}\]/i in className literals
- Replace the two sites with a surface token

## Expected impact
The repo hex ban covers Tailwind arbitrary values; may surface more warnings elsewhere.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - hex ban sees every hardcoded hex
Before: 2 of 4 hex sites in this context flagged
After: 4 of 4 flagged (probe: the regex matches both class strings)
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Stacking mutates particle objects that are already React state
instrument: test that freezes the previous particles array (Object.freeze each entry) and runs a stacking frame; throws today
body:
## Summary
The accumulate/merge branch edits existing.amount/stackCount/displayText in place on objects the last setParticles committed.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/DamageNumberPhysicsSimulator/useDamageNumberPhysicsSimulator.ts:83-96 mutates particlesRef.current entries, which are the same objects the previous render holds in `particles`. Today the next frame replaces them via updateParticle, so nothing visible breaks; under StrictMode double-invocation or a dropped frame the committed state shows a changed amount without a render. Fix: replace the entry immutably.

## Flow
- Accumulate preset, high attack rate
- previous particles state object amount changes between renders
- Fix: map to a new object for the stacked entry

## Expected impact
Removes a latent state-mutation hazard; no visible change expected.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no in-place mutation of committed state
Before: 2 branches mutate committed objects
After: 0
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
